clue.text: Comes in and records

definitions.meaning: first meaning: goes into a place, verb
second meaning: writes down in a register or ledger, verb

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one verb: walking into a room, and logging data in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both arriving inside somewhere and noting an item formally in a log or account.

clue.text: Taken away and prosecuted over second-rate pamphlet

indicators.note: in a down clue, one word lying over another can be wrapped round it, so these letters enclose the rest

parts.note: to be sued is to be prosecuted in a civil court
B, a B grade or B-movie, is second-rate
a tract is a short religious or political pamphlet

explanation.surface: Someone was charged in court for producing a shoddy leaflet, and the item was confiscated.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' can mean one piece wraps the other; B is the usual crossword letter for second-rate, as in a B-movie.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic a number taken away from another is subtracted; the phrase is the plain synonym for deducted.

clue.text: Flimsy bit of clothing

indicators.note: only a small piece of the next word is wanted, so the answer lies inside it

explanation.surface: A garment that is only a scrap of fabric is described as flimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Flimsy fabric is insubstantial and lightweight, which is what thin describes.

clue.text: Season with Italian football team

parts.note: Inter Milan, usually just Inter, is a Serie A football club

explanation.surface: A sports fan spends a part of the year following a club from Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: The cold quarter of the year is one of the four seasons of the calendar.

clue.text: Offered to stimulate into action about attitude

indicators.note: the first word goes round, about, the second

parts.note: to prod someone is to goad or stimulate them into action
a pose is a bodily attitude or a posture adopted for effect

explanation.surface: Someone volunteered to galvanise colleagues by tackling their poor outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A suggestion put forward for consideration has been proposed, i.e. tabled or put up for acceptance.

clue.text: Fantastic Four seen in new premises

indicators.note: the numeral is spotted inside the rearranged letters, so it goes within them
a new version of the word premises has its letters arranged afresh

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The Marvel superhero team, the Fantastic Four, have been spotted at a new building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic Four' looks like the comic-book team, but 'Fantastic' alone is the definition and 'Four' is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fantastic is remarkable or striking, which is what impressive means in everyday praise.

clue.text: Two calls for effort for indecisive person

indicators.note: two calls means the cry is given a second time, so the same letters are written out twice

parts.note: yo is a cry made when heaving or straining, as in yo-heave-ho

explanation.surface: A dithering person can only manage a couple of half-hearted shouts of encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: A yo-yo, in British usage, is someone who keeps changing their mind, going up and down like the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the toy on a string, a waverer swings back and forth between opinions without settling.

clue.text: Protected action involving ward

indicators.note: the first word takes in, involves, the second

parts.note: a deed is an action or act
to fend off is to ward off, so fend means ward

explanation.surface: A legal action concerned a child under guardianship and kept them safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ward' looks like a noun, a child in care, but here it is the verb as in ward off.
explanation.definitionFit: To have guarded or shielded something from attack is to have defended it.

clue.text: Name anything that is primarily randy and racier

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the first letter of randy

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to say anything that is chiefly lustful and more risque.
explanation.definitionFit: Racier jokes are more risque and suggestive, as are naughtier ones; both are comparative adjectives.

clue.text: Low sides of savage ungulate

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound cattle make

indicators.note: the sides of the word savage are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A hoofed animal is mooing ferociously on both flanks.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungulate is any hoofed mammal; this large deer of northern forests is one example.

clue.text: Former tinge is gone

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
a tinct is a tint or tinge of colour

explanation.surface: A colour that once tinted something has faded away.
explanation.definitionFit: A species that is gone from the earth, with no living members, has died out completely.

clue.text: Desired goal: post office in funds

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits in the word for funds

parts.note: a purse is a sum of money or funds, as in the public purse

explanation.surface: Someone states their aim: getting a post office into the budget.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or intention one wants to achieve is one's purpose, the end in view.

clue.text: Tolerate American ways and principles

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate or bear it
RDS is the abbreviation for roads, which are ways

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with US customs and values.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral standards are the rules of conduct a person lives by, their guiding beliefs.

clue.text: Abnormally deep loving evolving

indicators.note: the letters behave abnormally, falling out of their usual order into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A deeply affectionate relationship is changing in an unusual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something developing is growing and changing gradually over time, which is what evolving describes.

clue.text: Stitched up someone gutless getting married

indicators.note: with the guts, the inside letters, removed only the outer letters of someone remain

parts.note: to wed is to marry; wed is also the past participle, married

explanation.surface: A cowardly person was framed on their wedding day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitched up' suggests being framed, but here it is literal sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairing a tear with needle and thread means it has been sewn or stitched shut.

clue.text: Fierce eagles seen initially in uncultivated region

parts.note: wild means fierce or savage
erne is a crossword-familiar word for a sea eagle

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of seen

explanation.surface: Savage birds of prey have been spotted at first in untamed country.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilderness is wild land never farmed or settled by people.

clue.text: After test, donates — but not good causes

indicators.note: the second part comes after the first

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles

indicators.note: but not tells us to take the letter for good out of the word

parts.note: to donate is to give

explanation.surface: After passing a check, someone donates money, but not to worthy charities.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly roadworthiness test for cars. GIVES loses its G to leave IVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Motives are the reasons behind an action, i.e. what causes or drives someone to act.

clue.text: Related to movement, worked up but lacking energy

indicators.note: lacking tells us one letter is missing from the word

parts.note: someone emotional is worked up or agitated
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Something about motion gets agitated yet has no vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Motional is the adjective from motion, describing what pertains to moving.

clue.text: Spotted hut under mountains getting turned over

indicators.note: the hut sits under the other piece in a down entry
in a down clue, turned over means read upwards, so the mountains run backwards

parts.note: the Alps are the great mountain range of Europe
a shed is a simple hut

explanation.surface: A hut beneath mountain peaks is being overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'turned over' reads the mountains upwards, and 'under' places the hut below them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something splashed is marked with drops or blotches, i.e. spotted or speckled.

clue.text: Bored doctor, sick and regularly seedy

parts.note: ill means sick

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of seedy

explanation.surface: A doctor is weary, unwell and somewhat shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' looks like weary, but it means made a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: To have drilled through something is to have bored a hole in it, as with a drill bit.

clue.text: Going with the flow, admit I'd alarmed guards

indicators.note: the phrase guards, holds within it, the answer letters

explanation.surface: Someone who goes along with things confesses that the security staff were frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across admiT I'D ALarmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal water moves with the current of the tides, so it literally goes with the flow.

clue.text: Left sentries confused, they hear

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Guards were abandoned in a state of bewilderment, and they could hear things.
explanation.definitionFit: Listeners are those who pay attention to sound, an audience.

clue.text: Clandestine group will admit soldiers

indicators.note: the group lets the soldiers in, so their letters go inside

parts.note: a sect is a religious or political group
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British soldiers

explanation.surface: An underground cell agrees to let troops join.
explanation.definitionFit: A clandestine operation is done covertly, kept hidden from others.

clue.text: Small boys eating adult's dishes

indicators.note: the outer letters consume the inner one, so it goes inside

parts.note: lads are boys
A is the film classification for adult; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Little lads are tucking into a grown-up's meals.
explanation.walkthrough: A sits between S and LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Salads are cold dishes of mixed raw vegetables, each one a dish served at a meal.

clue.text: Officer commanding highest US influential organisation

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding
top means highest

explanation.surface: A commanding officer leads the most senior American body.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus is used figuratively for a powerful organisation with many far-reaching tentacles of influence.

clue.text: Closely follow story we're told

indicators.note: we are told something by hearing it spoken, so the word is heard not seen

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: We are told a narrative to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail a suspect is to shadow them, as a detective does.

clue.text: Designer adopts new means of communication

indicators.note: the designer takes in, adopts, the letter so it goes inside

parts.note: Coco Chanel was a celebrated French fashion designer

explanation.surface: A fashion designer takes up a novel way of getting a message across.
explanation.definitionFit: A channel is a route or medium through which information is conveyed.

clue.text: Cunning masonry construction

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as in sly, knowing or roguish
second meaning: a curved structure of stone or brick spanning an opening

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both a sly adjective and a curved stone structure.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch look is knowing and mischievous; an arch is a curved span built of stone or brick.

clue.text: A legal right to retain property from elsewhere

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A legal entitlement to keep goods belonging to someone from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alien is foreign, coming from another place or world.

clue.text: Worked out decree with six changes

indicators.note: the letters undergo changes, reordering into another word

explanation.surface: An edict was figured out after six amendments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked out' suggests solved, but it means trained physically.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who exercised has done physical training at the gym, a workout.
